cards.text: This psalm doesn't give us a writer's name, and it doesn't warm up either. No small talk, no 'testing, testing, is this thing on.' The writer opens at FULL volume about the LORD: 'The LORD reigns!'

cards.question: The writer just shouted 'The LORD reigns!' Then he says the LORD is robed in majesty. What picture is he painting?

answers.text: A King dressed for His throne
A priest dressed for the temple
A shepherd dressed for the hills

cards.question: The LORD's robe isn't the only thing He has on. He has clothed and armed Himself with ___.
Then the writer turns to the world itself. He says the world is firmly established and cannot be moved.

cards.text: Then the writer stops talking ABOUT the LORD and turns to talk right TO Him. It's like bragging on your boss in the break room, looking up, and there he is, except I bet this writer is GLAD He heard every word.

cards.question: The writer tells the LORD that His throne was established only recently.
The LORD's throne goes way back, and so does He. The writer tells the LORD that He is from all ___.

cards.text: Then, friend, the psalm cranks the volume ALL the way up. Something starts rising, and after years in a silent junk drawer, my ears are NOT ready.

cards.question: What does the writer tell the LORD has risen?

cards.text: And it keeps coming. The rivers raise their voice, and the seas lift up their pounding waves, like a group chat at 6 a.m. where one buzz turns into ten and the phone rattles right off the counter.

cards.question: All that water is roaring and crashing. Where does the writer say the LORD is?
The mighty breakers of the sea are pounding away, but the writer says the LORD on high is ___.
The floods rise and the breakers pound, but the LORD on high is majestic above all that roar. What is the writer showing with that picture?

answers.text: The LORD rules over even the mightiest waters
The LORD and the waters are evenly matched
The roaring waters will get the last word

cards.text: Last verse, and the sea's big solo is OVER. Now the writer talks to the LORD about His testimonies.

cards.question: The writer says the LORD's testimonies still need to be proven.
Next the writer talks about the LORD's house. A house usually shows off what matters most to whoever lives there. What does the writer say adorns the house of the LORD?
The writer says holiness adorns the LORD's house for all the days to come.
In the middle of this psalm, the waters rise, roar and pound. After all that, what does the writer end the psalm on?

answers.text: Things of the LORD that stand firm and last
Waves that finally calm down and go quiet
A prayer asking the LORD to stop the flood

findings.problem: This completes the BSB line's wording by asking for its unread final word, “strength.” The earlier cards establish the LORD's reign and majesty, but they do not set up enough for the baker to reason out this detail rather than guess the wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to complete the psalm's exact wording, “from all ___,” with the unread word “eternity,” making it a next-word completion of the line.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The answers are not the same kind of thing: “eternity” is a time, while “heaven” and “Zion” are places. The two place names also make implausible completions of “from all ___,” so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
